title: The Clinic slice
goal: A crew of up to four rides the elevator into a bright two-level Clinic floor, finds the Orderly, takes a reading, and banks or rides down.
nowText: Adding a job that publishes every green build to GitHub Pages, then switching Pages on.

tasks.title: Project setup
tasks.why: The tools that build, test and publish the game, and the live link.
tasks.summary: Typecheck, 7 rule tests and the build pass. The browser test boots the game on this PC's graphics card and its screenshot was looked at. CI and a secret scan run on every push.

media.caption: The very first frame: a placeholder corridor at the game's low internal resolution

tasks.title: The Clinic floor generator
tasks.why: Every floor is built from a seed, so every player gets the same building and no two runs match.
tasks.summary: 29 tests pass over 800 generated floors (200 seeds at four depths): every room reachable from the elevator, two levels joined by a stair, an atrium, dead-end side branches, a corridor loop and long sight lines. Fable re-ran the checks and read a printed map.

media.caption: Printed map of one floor, lower then upper level

tasks.title: Walking through a floor
tasks.why: The first time the game is a place you can move around in, in first person.
tasks.summary: You can walk a generated two-level Clinic floor in first person: corridors, rooms with door gaps, a stair, and a balcony over the atrium. 48 rule tests pass, including collision. A browser test walks from the elevator up the stair to the balcony, and a second one presses real keys: W walks, Shift creeps, a wall stops you. Fable re-ran everything and looked at the screenshots. Lighting is flat and the rooms are empty; mouse look is not tested.

media.caption: A 48-metre corridor, the kind of sight line you will first see the Orderly down
Looking down into the atrium from the upper balcony
The atrium from below, two storeys tall
Where you step out of the elevator

tasks.title: A public play link on GitHub Pages
tasks.why: You said yes: every green build also goes to a public link friends can open from anywhere.

tasks.title: AGPL-3.0 licence
tasks.why: You chose it for the public repository.
tasks.summary: The AGPL-3.0 licence text is in the repository and the README says so.

tasks.title: The Orderly, second pass
tasks.why: The first entity. The first pass reads as a mannequin; this pass has to make it frightening in bright light.

media.caption: First pass, as a player would meet it
First pass poses: idle, walk, walk, reach, frozen
First pass at game resolution: the smile is lost

todo: First, study: the agent goes through two YouTube Blender tutorials on making horror characters or low-detail retro creatures (their transcripts plus frames sampled from the video), and writes what it learned to docs/ART-NOTES.md before touching the model.

Apply it, with your answers: taller so it ducks under door frames; a body under the gown (ribs, spine, collarbones, real elbows and wrists); the printed smile much bigger and bolder; something wrong where the eyes should be; longer, more articulated hands; less funny, more frightening.
Load it in the game on a Clinic floor and check the reach and the walk there.
Revision round 1: blind judges (fresh Opus agents shown only the pictures) and Fable each say what they see and what looks cheap; the agent fixes the worst of it.
Revision round 2: the same again on the fixed figure. Pictures from every round go on this page.

tasks.title: The tape-playback look and the debug overlay
tasks.why: The degraded recovered-footage look that hides rough art, plus tools for testing.

tasks.title: Stronger checks
tasks.why: So a regression is caught by a machine, not by luck: reference screenshots that fail the test when the picture changes, a frame-time limit inside the browser test, a smoke test for the hub, and a deliberate-break check on every gate already passed.

tasks.title: The Orderly comes alive
tasks.why: It walks the floor, is heard before it is seen, and never moves while anyone is watching it.

tasks.title: The instrument, the recording rule and tapes
tasks.why: How the crew earns: readings only record the scary part, and the tape has to be carried out.

tasks.title: The elevator
tasks.why: The only safe place. Calling it, waiting out its loud arrival, then bank or ride down.

tasks.title: The elevator voice
tasks.why: The relentlessly cheerful announcer, recorded with ElevenLabs, with an audition page for you.

tasks.title: Playing together
tasks.why: Four players in one building over a peer-to-peer connection, with one player hosting.

tasks.title: Bot crewmates and the test panel
tasks.why: So you can test a full crew alone on the live link.

tasks.title: Going down, cameras and the wipe
tasks.why: Being caught puts you on the cameras, and a full wipe ends the run.

tasks.title: The shadow trigger
tasks.why: A shadow crossing a doorway in a quiet moment: a scare trigger, never the monster.

tasks.title: Frame rate
tasks.why: Measured on this PC with four players, then fixed until it is smooth.

tasks.title: Final validation
tasks.why: A fresh reviewer audits everything against the gates and the fairness rules.

tasks.title: More than one floor skeleton
tasks.why: Every Clinic floor shares one skeleton today, which will feel samey by the third floor.

tasks.title: Stretch: voice that fades with distance, a second trait, the Tenant, a second place
tasks.why: Only if every gate is green with time left.

decisions.text: Pinned Vite 6 and Vitest 3 to suit the Node already on this PC, not upgrading Node.
Repository licence: none yet (question "license" on the hub).
The North Star design document stays out of the public repository (question "publish-design-doc").

feed.text: Started T0b: A public play link on GitHub Pages. Adding a job that publishes every green build to GitHub Pages, then switching Pages on.
Finished T2a: Walking through a floor.
Added two standing rules: break a thing on purpose to prove its test can fail before ticking a gate, and check anything live from a second device.
You asked for the Orderly's second pass to start with tutorial study and end with two judged revision rounds. It now comes right after the public play link.
The Progress page was rebuilt: a roadmap of steps that fill with their own pictures, an overall bar, and a strip of the newest output.

Your answers are in: the setting (a civilisation that kept building upward, with convicts sent down to buy their freedom), the name stays Going Down, all five places, six candidate mechanics including the fake-disconnect and fake-restart, 50,000 voice characters, AGPL, and a public play link.
Added task T0b: A public play link on GitHub Pages.

Started T2a: Walking through a floor. An Opus agent is building it: collision as tested logic, the floor as real geometry, the bright Clinic look, and a browser test that walks from the elevator up the stair to the balcony.
The hub is live on the tailnet and linked from the home dashboard.
CI's first full run failed (the browser test could not find the preview server on Linux). Fixed and green since.
New pictures for T3: The Orderly, second pass.
Gate G2 (Floors are sound) is passed.
Finished T1: The Clinic floor generator.
The loop started. Public repository created; secret scanning on every commit and push.
